column1: What Lie About Your Worth Do You Believe?
column5: The "I'm Too Much" Lie | The "I'm Not Enough" Lie | The "I'm Unlovable" Lie | The "I Have to Earn It" Lie
column6: Names the exact lie running your self-talk, then answers it with who God says you are; the lie label is screenshot-bait people repost as a confession.
column8: Devotional corpus on "lies the enemy tells" (Proverbs31 "Shame Doesn't Get the Final Say", Seedword "10 biggest lies of the enemy", renew.org "Our Identity and the Enemy") centers on lies like "you're not good enough / not lovable / too flawed"; "feeling not good enough" is a top Christian search.

column1: Who Are You in Christ, Really?
column5: Chosen | Beloved | Redeemed | Sealed and Secure
column6: Turns the most-searched Christian identity question into a personal badge ("I'm Beloved") instead of a sermon; "who am I in Christ" is an evergreen high-volume query.
column8: Who am I in Christ returns massive results (Cru, Joyce Meyer, Navigators, Bible Study Tools 20+ verses, "28 I AM statements"); Cru/biblestudytools frame identity as chosen/loved/accepted/enough.

column1: What's Your Comparison Trap?
column5: The Highlight-Reel Scroller | The Silent Scorekeeper | The Never-Measures-Up | The Secret Competitor
column6: Diagnoses HOW you compare (not whether), making "comparison is the thief of joy" personal and shareable for the social-media generation.
column8: Comparison is the thief of joy is a huge Christian sermon topic (Desiring God, Christianity Today, Perspective Ministries); sources tie it to social media envy, "smug pride or envious inferiority", and feeling "less in the end".

column1: What's Your Loneliness Pattern?
column5: Emotional Loneliness | Social Loneliness | Existential Loneliness | Situational Loneliness
column6: Maps your loneliness onto the real psychological types so it feels named and validated, then points each to a biblical companion; deeply shareable for the "I feel this" crowd.
column8: Psychology Today / iPractice / Oxford Gerontologist define emotional, social, existential (plus situational/chronic) loneliness as distinct types; "what kind of lonely are you" is a recognized framing.

column1: Which Overlooked Bible Person Are You?
column5: Leah (the unseen one) | Hagar (the cast-out one) | Mephibosheth (the forgotten one) | Zacchaeus (the outsider)
column6: Flagship archetype for people who feel invisible; each result is someone God SAW and chose, turning "I'm overlooked" into "I'm seen". Pure identity-badge energy.
column8: Multiple "overlooked/forgotten/underappreciated Bible characters" roundups (Mockingbird, AnsweredFaith, Crossway "5 forgotten women") center Leah ("wanted to be seen"), Hagar ("the God who sees me"), Mephibosheth, Zacchaeus.

column1: Are You a Leah or a Rachel?
column5: Leah (overlooked but chosen) | Rachel (loved but striving)
column6: A binary "which sister" quiz in the proven Mary-or-Martha mold, but about being the unseen one vs the envied one; instantly debatable and shareable.
column8: Bible.org titles Leah "The Woman No Man Loved But Every Woman Envied"; teaching corpus frames the Leah/Rachel rivalry as overlooked-vs-favored, a built-in comparison dyad.

column1: What's Your Hidden Insecurity?
column5: Fear of Being Found Out | Fear of Not Mattering | Fear of Rejection | Fear of Falling Behind
column6: Surfaces the insecurity you mask, with a gentle scripture reframe; "the thing I never say out loud" framing drives private shares and saves.
column8: Identity-in-Christ resources (Cru, Esther Dorotik "Overcoming the Lies Lurking Within") name hidden fears of being unlovable/not enough; "feeling not good enough" and impostor feelings are recurring Christian struggles.

column1: Do You Have Christian Impostor Syndrome?
column5: The Fraud Feeling | The Never-Holy-Enough | The Comparison Christian | The Secure-in-Grace
column6: Names the "I'm faking my faith / everyone's holier than me" feeling so many carry silently; the diagnosis itself is the shareable hook.
column8: Identity/lies devotionals describe believers feeling "you've committed too many sins, God can't really love you"; impostor-style "am I a real Christian / not holy enough" is a common quiet struggle surfaced in identity content.

column1: What's Stealing Your Sense of Worth?
column5: Achievement | Approval | Appearance | Other People's Opinions
column6: Pinpoints the idol your worth is hooked to, then redirects it to grace; "stop letting X define you" is endlessly quotable.
column8: Cru/finds.life.church identity content warns the world defines you by "looks, achievements, or followers"; Romans 15:7 framing ("you don't need approval/validation from the world") is widely cited.

column1: Which "Unseen by God" Moment Do You Relate To?
column5: Hagar in the Wilderness | Elijah Under the Broom Tree | Hannah at the Temple | David in the Caves
column6: For the person who feels God forgot them; each story ends with God showing up, reframing "does God even see me" into "He sees me". High emotional pull.
column8: Hagar's "You are the God who sees me" (El Roi) is a headline theme in overlooked-character studies; "feeling unseen by God / forgotten" is a documented loneliness-and-faith struggle.

column1: What's Your Belonging Style?
column5: The Outsider Looking In | The Always-Almost-In | The Lone Wolf by Habit | The Quietly Connected
column6: Diagnoses why connection feels hard for you, validating church-loneliness without blame; "belong before you believe" makes it warm and shareable.
column8: Crossway "Feeling Alone in a Crowded Congregation" and "Belong. Believe. Behave" describe belonging styles and the outsider experience; "it's hard to trust when you feel like an outsider" is a core theme.

column1: Why Is It So Hard for You to Make Friends?
column5: You Wait to Be Chosen | You Fear the First Move | You Keep It Surface | You're Spread Too Thin
column6: Names your specific friendship blocker, an enormous adult/Christian pain point, with one tiny biblical next step; "this is literally me" energy.
column8: How to make friends as an adult is a major topic (Psychology Today, Gospel Coalition, Crosswalk "10 Ways to Make Friends if You're Lonely at Church"); share of US adults with no close friends quadrupled to 12% since 1990.

column1: Which Bible Friendship Do You Long For?
column5: David and Jonathan | Ruth and Naomi | Paul and Timothy | Jesus and His Inner Three
column6: Lets the friend-starved pick the bond they crave; aspirational and gift-able to a friend ("you're my Jonathan"). Distinct from a friendship-type sorter.
column8: Adult-friendship and church-loneliness corpus repeatedly invokes biblical friendship as the antidote; David/Jonathan, Ruth/Naomi, Paul/Timothy are the canonical Christian friendship models.

column1: What's Your Self-Worth Source?
column5: Performance-Based | Approval-Based | Comparison-Based | Grace-Based
column6: Reveals the foundation your worth stands on and whether it can hold; the "grace-based" goal-state makes people want to share and aspire.
column8: Identity-in-Christ teaching contrasts striving/performance/approval worth with grace ("you don't have to strive to be accepted by God", Romans 15:7); a foundational Christian self-worth theme.

column1: Which Lie From the Mirror Do You Believe?
column5: I'm Not Pretty Enough | "I'm Too Much" | "I'm Forgettable" | "I'll Never Be Enough"
column6: Tackles appearance/body-image insecurity head-on with a tender truth reframe; raw, confessional, and highly shareable among women especially.
column8: Comparison sermons cite "filtered beauty standards leading to eating disorders/self-harm"; body-image and "not pretty/good enough" are explicit threads in comparison and identity content.

column1: What's Your Social-Media Comparison Type?
column5: The Doom-Scroller | The Curator | The Lurker-Comparer | The FOMO Feeler
column6: Hyper-current quiz on how the feed messes with your worth; named types are instantly tag-a-friend material for the most relatable modern struggle.
column8: Comparison-thief-of-joy sources directly blame social media for envy/depression and "feeling down on ourselves"; social-media comparison is the dominant modern form of the comparison struggle.

column1: Which "Found by God" Story Is Yours?
column5: The Prodigal Who Came Home | Zacchaeus in the Tree | The Lost Sheep | The Woman at the Well
column6: For anyone who's felt lost or far off; the "God came looking for ME" payoff is profoundly moving and shareable. Belonging through being sought.
column8: Second-chance/belonging corpus centers the prodigal son, Zacchaeus ("you belong with me" before he changed), and the lost sheep/coin/son ("Jesus came to seek and save the lost").

column1: Are You Living From Approval or Acceptance?
column5: The Approval Chaser | The People-Pleaser | The Performer | The Already-Accepted
column6: A sharp two-state mirror that exposes the exhausting approval treadmill vs resting in being accepted; "stop performing for love" is deeply quotable.
column8: Identity resources stress you already have "the stamp of approval from Him" and never have to "try harder for Him to love you more" (Joyce Meyer, Romans 15:7); approval-vs-acceptance is a core identity tension.

column1: What's Your Inner Critic's Favorite Lie?
column5: You're a Failure | "You're Unlovable" | "You Don't Belong" | "You're Stuck Forever"
column6: Personifies the negative voice and names its go-to line, then silences it with truth; the "my inner critic says ___" hook is share-and-relate gold.
column8: Seedword/renew.org list enemy lies almost verbatim ("you're stuck and hopeless", "you aren't lovable"); the inner-critic / shame voice is a defining identity struggle in this corpus.

column1: Which Outsider Woman of the Bible Are You?
column5: The Woman at the Well | Hagar | Ruth the Foreigner | The Bleeding Woman
column6: For women who feel on the margins; each was an outsider Jesus/God moved toward. Distinct from generic woman-of-the-Bible by its "outsider/unseen" lens.
column8: Crossway "5 Stories of Forgotten Women", Almost Heretical and HISsparrow lists spotlight marginalized women (woman at the well, Hagar, Ruth, the bleeding woman) as outsiders God sees and includes.

column1: What Does Your Loneliness Need Right Now?
column5: Deep Connection | A Community | To Be Truly Known | God's Presence
column6: Reframes loneliness from a flaw into an unmet need with a next step; gentle, practical, and shareable as "this is what I actually needed to hear".
column8: Gospel Coalition "The Christian Cure for Loneliness Isn't Just More Friends" distinguishes needs (being known/loved vs more contacts); maps onto emotional vs social vs existential loneliness types.

column1: What's Your "Not Enough" Story?
column5: Not Smart Enough | Not Holy Enough | Not Successful Enough | Not Wanted Enough
column6: Pinpoints the specific flavor of "not enough" you carry and rewrites the ending with grace; the universal "not enough" hook is irresistibly relatable.
column8: Not good enough / not enough is the single most cited identity lie across Cru, Daughter of Delight, and identity-verse roundups ("You are enough in Christ"); a top emotional driver.

column1: Which Hidden-Hero of the Bible Matches You?
column5: Epaphras (the prayer warrior) | Onesimus (the second-chance one) | Andrew (the quiet connector) | The Boy With the Loaves
column6: For people who feel small or behind-the-scenes; celebrates unseen faithfulness. Distinct from apostle/character quizzes by its "obscure but vital" angle.
column8: Roundups of "obscure / lesser-known / underappreciated Bible characters" (AnsweredFaith, Rambling Everon "The Invisibles", Mockingbird) spotlight background figures whose small acts mattered.

column1: Are You the Older Brother or the Prodigal?
column5: The Prodigal (came home wrecked) | The Older Brother (stayed but resentful)
column6: A binary self-test from the most famous parable, exposing both the shame path AND the secret-resentment path; debatable, convicting, shareable.
column8: Parable of the Prodigal Son (Wikipedia, Diana Leagh Matthews) is one of the best-known second-chance stories; the older-brother resentment angle is a classic, less-discussed self-recognition.

column1: What's Your Belonging Wound?
column5: The Always-Left-Out | The Never-Picked | The Different One | The Drifted-Away
column6: Names the early experience behind why belonging feels unsafe, with compassion and hope; "wound" framing is vulnerable and high-resonance.
column8: Belonging begins with noticing who's missing and church-cliques/"full of cliques" content (Equipping Godly Women, Augustana) describe left-out and outsider wounds that shape adult belonging.

column1: Which Insecurity Is Holding You Back?
column5: Fear of Judgment | Fear of Failure | Fear of Not Belonging | Fear of Being Seen
column6: Action-oriented insecurity diagnosis with a freedom-focused result; "what's secretly holding me back" is strong self-improvement + faith crossover.
column8: Identity content (Cru, 412teens) ties insecurity/fear to not stepping into your identity; "confidence grows, shame and fear lose their grip" is the promised payoff in identity-in-Christ resources.

column1: How Do You Handle Feeling Left Out?
column5: You Withdraw | You Overcompensate | You Numb It | You Pretend You're Fine
column6: Maps your coping move when excluded, validating a universal sting with a healthier path; "feeling left out" is broadly relatable and confessional.
column8: Church-loneliness corpus (Crossway "Feeling Alone in a Crowded Congregation", cliques articles) describes feeling left out despite being present; coping responses (withdraw/mask) are common threads.

column1: Whose Worth Are You Trying to Borrow?
column5: The Influencer | The Achiever Friend | The "Perfect" Christian | The Highlight Reel
column6: A novel angle on comparison: who you're measuring against to feel okay; the unexpected framing gives it scroll-stopping novelty.
column8: Comparison sources describe envying others' lives "wishing ours was the same" and chasing others' standards; borrowing worth from comparison targets is a fresh, accurate spin on the documented behavior.

column1: Who Sees You When You Feel Invisible?
column5: El Roi, the God Who Sees (Hagar) | Jesus Who Stopped (Bartimaeus) | The Father Watching the Road | The Shepherd Who Searches
column6: Comfort-first quiz for the invisible-feeling; lands on a name/image of God who notices YOU. Deeply emotional, save-and-share devotional energy.
column8: Hagar's El Roi "God who sees me", the father "watching the road" for the prodigal, and the searching shepherd recur across belonging/overlooked-character sources as answers to feeling unseen.

column1: Identity in Christ IQ: Do You Know Who You Are?
column5: Rooted (deep) | Growing | Shaky | Just Starting
column6: A knowledge quiz on the "I am" scriptures (chosen, redeemed, sealed) that doubles as encouragement; pairs the popular identity topic with a learn-the-verses hook.
column8: Navigators/Northwoods/notebookandpenguin compile "I AM" identity statements and verses to memorize (1 Peter 2:9, Gal 2:20, Zeph 3:17); strong demand for knowing identity scriptures, lower virality as knowledge.

column1: Comparison or Contentment: Which Verse Wins?
column5: Contentment Master | Mostly Free | Often Snared | Comparison-Bound
column6: A "guess/choose the verse" game on comparison vs contentment (1 Cor 13:4, Gal 6:4, Phil 4:11); rides the comparison topic with a light competitive format.
column8: Comparison corpus cites "love does not envy" (1 Cor 13:4), Gal 6:4 ("test your own work"), and contentment verses; demand exists but knowledge format caps shareability.
